question: Within a bounded v1.3 static read set, does wonder item 206, Great Library of Alexandria, reach an exact technology-ownership read or write, generic technology acquisition, completion consumer, display consumer, or AI consumer?

scope.boundary: This packet tests exact references and split-address materialization for the Great Library record, description, cost cell, technology table, ownership bitsets, and accepted technology helpers, then scans decoded literal or comparison uses of item 206 and decompiles exactly the three emitted functions. It does not expand truncated bodies, inspect unrelated callers, search every wonder or technology consumer, reconstruct display, or claim executable-wide absence.

dependencies.use: Provides exact item 206 identity, record, effect-description text, and signed cost factor.
Provides the ordinary BuildingWonderProductionCostLookup path that is excluded from effect evidence.
Provides accepted technology table, ownership, eligibility, and acquisition anchors without making them Great Library effects.

acceptedAnchors.qualification: The English effect description is a discovery hint, not proof of technology transfer.

referenceScan.qualification: The generic helper references reproduce accepted technology-system calls but carry no item-206 or Great-Library-record edge. Zero reference-manager results do not prove absence from undecoded or split-constant paths.

splitAddressScan.negative: No decoded split construction matched the exact Great Library record, description, cost cell, or technology ownership-bitset base. The sole match was the already-accepted generic technology-table materializer.

itemIdScan.result: The complete filtered decoded-instruction scan emitted three functions, each using 0xCE as a literal argument rather than a proved wonder identity.

candidateResults.result: The recovered prefix uses 0xCE as a physics diagnostic argument in a scene spring-and-damper path.
candidateResults.stop: The function has no Great Library or technology carrier and truncates on bad instruction data.

candidateResults.result: The recovered prefix exposes no Great Library, technology, completion, display, or AI carrier before its literal site.
candidateResults.stop: The exact function body truncates on bad instruction data, so expansion is forbidden.

candidateResults.result: The recovered prefix is a counted-entry removal routine and exposes no Great Library or technology carrier.
candidateResults.stop: The exact function body truncates on bad instruction data.

ordinaryCostBoundary.result: The accepted item-206 cost path remains ordinary wonder production-cost evidence and is not treated as completion or effect consumption.
ordinaryCostBoundary.qualification: Cost selection alone cannot prove technology transfer, completion, display, or AI behavior.

boundedNegative.result: The completed bounded read set does not establish an exact Great-Library-to-technology-ownership, technology-acquisition, completion, display, or AI edge.
boundedNegative.limits: This negative covers the eight exact reference targets, five split-address targets, the complete three-function filtered scalar result, and the recovered prefixes of 0x8286FD70, 0x82951B58, and 0x829C1298. It does not classify any undecoded, indirect, record-indexed, dynamically dispatched, or unsearched function.
boundedNegative.falsificationCondition: A complete exact function or independently bounded dataflow joins item 206 or Great-Library-record-derived state to technology ownership or acquisition, completion, display, or AI consumption.

currentEvidence.method: Four successful sequential foreground read-only Ghidra queries: exact references, capped split constants, a filtered item-206 scalar-use scan, and three exact candidate decompilations.

entries.result: The record, description, cost, technology-table, ownership-bitset, and acquisition targets have zero reference-manager entries; ownership and eligibility helpers expose only the listed generic direct calls.
Only the generic technology table was materialized; the eight-function-cap scan did not truncate.
Exactly three filtered literal uses were emitted and the scan did not truncate.
All three candidates lack a proved Great Library technology edge and all exact bodies truncate on bad instruction data, activating the packet stop.

currentEvidence.qualification: The Ghidra project and flat image match the accepted v1.3 contract and were queried read-only without a project lock. No generated-code discovery, runtime probe, or indirect-target inference was used.

guards: Do not claim that no Great Library consumer exists outside the bounded read set.
Do not infer technology transfer from the English effect description.
Do not treat ordinary cost selection through 0x82CF1278 as completion or effect evidence.
Do not reinterpret unrelated literal 0xCE uses as item identity without a separate carrier.
Do not expand truncated functions, dynamic dispatch, unresolved writers, display reconstruction, runtime behavior, save or network behavior, or implementation design.
conclusion: The bounded v1.3 static read set did not establish an exact Great Library technology-ownership, technology-acquisition, completion, display, or AI edge. Exact and split-address scans exposed only generic technology helpers and a technology-table materializer. The complete filtered item-206 scan yielded three unrelated or unproved literal uses, and all three exact candidate bodies truncate on bad instruction data. This is not an executable-wide absence claim.
